journal_file_before_reopen.note: journal left by the killed transaction has a zeroed header (magic never synced at commit) -> NOT hot; SQLite ignores it and the DB file on disk was never dirtied pre-commit, so atomicity holds structurally

s3_crash_atomicity_a.verdict: uncommitted run row R999 absent; committed claim+project rows survived; quick_check ok. Leftover -journal file is inert (non-hot) garbage — harmless, next transaction overwrites it

s4_kill_midcommit_b.question: kill (taskkill /T /F) during 200 sequential committed create_claim mutations; DB must reopen clean with consistent counts
s4_kill_midcommit_b.invariant: after every kill+reopen: PRAGMA quick_check='ok' AND count(pending_binding_claims) == count(events WHERE kind='binding_claim_created') — each committed create_claim writes exactly one claim row + one event in a single transaction, so a torn commit must show up as a count mismatch or a failed quick_check
s4_kill_midcommit_b.note: this machine completes the 200-mutation loop in ~0.6s, so besides the random 0.5-2s delay kills, one deterministic attempt kills the child after a read-only connection witnesses >=50 committed claims, guaranteeing the kill lands mid-commit-loop

s6_networkfs_negative_d.caveat: a *reachable* SMB share would still be openable by raw SQLite (see raw_sqlite3_connect): the network-FS ban is a zloop policy obligation (VOL-07 §2), not something the engine enforces for us; the unreachable-UNC case fails closed at the filesystem layer

decision: journal_mode=DELETE, synchronous=EXTRA for this machine (VOL-07 §3 v1 default path / D-1 path (c)): the runtime sqlite 3.50.4 is inside the WAL-reset affected range (3.7.0-3.51.2, below the 3.50.7 backport), and pysqlite3 — though it installs cleanly on cp314/Windows (wheel exists) — bundles sqlite 3.51.1, which is still inside the affected range, so fix path (a) does not lift the gate today. WAL is forbidden until the version gate passes (I22); zloop doctor must warn 'WAL available after SQLite upgrade (see VOL-07 §3)'. Remaining upgrade route: path (b) — bundle the sqlite.org 3.53.4 DLL and load it explicitly once a gate-passing build is wired in. Until then S relies on DELETE+EXTRA with hot-journal rollback semantics, which this probe validated under crash/kill/contention.
